question: How do Django REST Framework serializers work and what is the difference between Serializer and ModelSerializer?
title: DRF Serializers vs ModelSerializer
direct_answer: Serializers convert between Python objects and JSON. ModelSerializer auto-generates fields from a Django model (like ModelForm for APIs) — specify model and fields in Meta. Serializer is manual — define each field explicitly, useful for non-model data or complex transformations. Both: validate() for cross-field validation, validate_<field>() for per-field validation, create() and update() for write operations.
interviewer_intent: Tests DRF core knowledge — serializers are the heart of every DRF API.

sections.title: Serializer vs ModelSerializer
sections.content:
ModelSerializer is the 90% case: it reads your Django model and generates serializer fields automatically. You specify which fields to include or exclude. create() and update() are auto-implemented to create or save model instances.

Serializer is for custom shapes: API responses that combine multiple models, non-database data, or complex transformations. You define each Field manually and implement create()/update() if needed.

Validation: field-level with validate_<field_name>(self, value) — raise ValidationError. Cross-field with validate(self, data) — receives all data after per-field validation.

seo.metaTitle: DRF Serializers vs ModelSerializer — Validation and Nested Relationships
seo.metaDescription: Django REST Framework serializers: ModelSerializer for model-backed APIs, custom Serializer for complex data, field-level and cross-field validation patterns.

speakable_v2.hook: DRF serializers are two things in one: a validation layer and a transformation layer.

beats.content: ModelSerializer reads your model and generates fields. Specify model and fields in Meta. create() and update() are auto-implemented. Custom create() for password hashing, audit logging, etc.
validate_<field>() for per-field custom rules. validate() for cross-field logic — it receives all fields after per-field validation. Raise serializers.ValidationError from both.
Nested serializers: author = UserSerializer(read_only=True) embeds the full user object. For write operations, nested writable serializers need custom create() and update().

speakable_v2.cap: write_only=True for passwords and tokens — never serialize sensitive fields in the response. The opposite, read_only=True, prevents callers from setting server-managed fields like id.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with SerializerMethodField for computed fields, or DRF's source= for renaming fields.
